title: Topology-aware KV hot-slab federation and eviction protocol for multi-GPU pipeline/tensor parallelism
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: As continuous batching increases, we observe KV cache working-set fragmentation across tensor/pipeline parallel boundaries. This causes uneven GPU memory pressure and tail-latency spikes when hot KV entries are replicated or moved without topology awareness. Goal: Design a federation + eviction protocol that shards 'hot slabs' across GPUs with knowledge of tensor/pipeline parallel mappings, so that hot-key locality is preserved for in-flight batched requests while minimizing cross-device transfers and stalls.
proposed_approach: 1) Hot-slab federation: classify KV slabs as cold/warm/hot using a decayed access counter per logical slab. 2) Topology hints: propagate tensor/pipeline mapping metadata (model shard id, pipeline stage id) with requests so the runtime can prefer colocated slabs. 3) Affinity table: maintain a lightweight per-node slab->GPU affinity that biases allocation and prefetch decisions. 4) Eviction protocol: multi-queue eviction with fast local eviction for capacity pressure and cooperative migration for changing hotspots; use conditional prefetch when pipeline stage changes are predicted. 5) Continuous batching integration: batch scheduler tags requests with stage/topology and requests are coalesced preferentially to GPUs holding the hot slabs; fallback routing allowed if SLOs require it.
tradeoffs_considered:
- Strong replication of hot slabs reduces tail latency but increases overall memory use and synchronization traffic.
- Strict locality enforcement reduces cross-GPU traffic but can cause hotspots to run out of memory; we plan soft-affinity (bias) instead of hard pinning.
- Migration vs. replication: migration saves memory but adds stalls; replication uses space but supports instant locality. We'll use LRU with replication threshold for very hot slabs.
acceptance_criteria:
- End-to-end benchmark: 99th percentile token latency under realistic continuous-batching mixes improves by >=15% vs baseline without topology hints.
- Overall additional GPU memory overhead for replication stays <8% on average for synthetic hotspot traces.
- No regressions in throughput (QPS) beyond 5% for common request mixes.
- Integration tests: tensor/pipeline boundary tests (unit & integration) that simulate stage handoffs and confirm no stale KV reads.
milestones: Integration with continuous batcher and synthetic benchmarks (week 3)
Internal canary on dedicated cluster + metrics (week 4)
notes: Sim harness: /bench/kv-hotspot-sim (NFS) — uses mixed sequence-length traces
open_questions: Preferred decay window for hotness signal across mixed-length sequences? (per-step or per-token?)
How to handle multi-tenant noisy neighbors when one tenant's hotset dominates memory?
Should replication be tenant-scoped (replicate within tenant set) or global?
implementation_plan: Phase A: lightweight affinity table + biasing in allocator; add hotness counters and local eviction. Phase B: cooperative migration and conditional replication threshold with background sync. Phase C: scheduler integration to preferentially route batches and experiments to measure tradeoffs. Each phase gated by benchmark thresholds and a canary run on dedicated pool.
risks: Mis-tuned hotness thresholds can thrash memory and increase tail latency.
Topology metadata adds small request overhead; need to ensure it doesn't perturb throughput.
Cross-GPU synchronization for replication state may increase PCIe/NCCL pressure on noisy interconnects.
testing_plan: Unit tests for affinity table and hotness decay. Microbenchmarks for single-GPU vs multi-GPU hotspot scenarios. End-to-end canary with real inference models (Llama-variant 13B) using continuous-batching harness. Canary to run with feature flag and telemetry enabled for 72 hours before gradual rollout.
metrics_to_track: GPU memory utilization variance across devices
batch hit rate for hot slabs
